sources.role: the answers to the two notification view header questions the 25 November re-distil raised from ruling:sam-2026-11-19 point 2. It settles c-438: once the amend confirmation page exists, 'Amend this notification' on the header is a link to that page rather than a posting button, because the first click then changes nothing, a POST that only renders a page is the wrong verb and leaves a re-POST on the back button without JavaScript, and Delete already opens its confirmation page by href in the same header; Copy as new keeps its own form because it still changes something, Delete stays a link, and no action shares another's form, in live animals, germinal products and plants alike. Point 2 of the 19 November ruling is unweakened, its subject being that no action shares another action's form, which a link does not do. It settles c-447 the other way from the default: the plants header gains a Copy as new action so both journeys offer the same three actions. That is wiring rather than a feature build, because every layer beneath it is already on main - the plants backend serves POST /{referenceNumber}/copy with a NotificationCopyMapper, the plants frontend's real and stub persistence both implement copy, and its engine holds copyJourney - and only the header's copyAction and route are missing. The plants backend therefore needs nothing and trade-imports-plants-backend does not join this programme's repos; inc-123 takes plantsfrontend alongside backend, frontend and tests, and inc-124's stale-copy return takes plants too. Plants' copy carries plants' own answers, so the carried-over-trade against cleared-shipment split is read against plants' own fields rather than copied field for field.

sources.role: the decision that pagination is kept everywhere and that its earlier removal was an error: every address book list and every address picker pages, and no requirement says a list of an organisation's addresses is served or shown unpaginated. It drops req-611's 'unpaginated' clause and supersedes ruling:ian-2026-11-23 point 6 on that point alone, because that point's reasoning rested on the address book's list endpoint taking no role and so having to be read whole and paged for display, which is no longer true of the service: RequestedListFilters takes roles and searchRoles, AddressController lists one page at a time with page and pageSize, and ListPaging sets 1 to 100 defaulting to 25, exactly the bounds ruling:paul-2026-11-05 point 8 names. The role filter runs in the service before the page is cut, so paging the API cannot make it wrong, and Paul's point 8 stands in full. The rest of ruling:ian-2026-11-23 stands: the pickers page at eight, the one-page clause of inc-087's criteria 7, 8 and 9 stays dropped with req-594 and req-595, and the 'Selected address' restatement comes back with the paging. EUDPA-827 is the fix and has landed on the animals frontend's main. It settles conflict c-292 by keeping the plants contact picker's pagination and inset, and the contact picker pages at eight rather than five, confirmed by Ian the same day, so every picker in both journeys pages at the figure the INS address book list already uses and ruling:ian-2026-11-23 point 1 set for the other pickers.

sources.role: the decision on transporter management, outranking ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm on that point and lifting claim c-285: the address book manages transporters as per-organisation records, and adding one mid journey uses the address book hand-off already built for addresses (inc-077, inc-078, inc-080). A transporter is its own record in its own transporters collection inside the address book service, not the Address model; it has no roles and stores a private-or-commercial type instead; a commercial transporter country is forced to XI (Northern Ireland) with no reference-data lookup, while a private transporter keeps its choice of export country. Approved transporters are parked.

claims.statement: This ruling settles whether the service manages transporters at all and, if so, whether the address book or something else does - the question ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm point 5 (claim c-285) left blocked pending requirements.
claims.quote: On transporter management, which Sam's ruling of 9 October (afternoon) left blocked pending requirements — whether the service manages transporters at all and, if so, whether the address book or something else does (`ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm` point 5, claim c-285):
claims.note: answers the block ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm point 5 left, recorded there as claim c-285

claims.statement: The address book manages transporters, which are saved per organisation just like other addresses.
claims.quote: My decision is that the address book will manage the transporters, just like other addresses which are saved per organisation.

claims.statement: Adding a transporter uses the same pattern of moving to the address book mid journey that adding other addresses uses.
claims.quote: It will use the same pattern with moving to the address book mid journey, like other addresses when adding transporters - it's essentially the same pattern.

claims.statement: The earlier block rested on the concept of 'approved transporters': a list that may be managed in MDM for all organisations and added to each organisation's own transporter options.
claims.quote: I think that previous ruling was based on the concept of 'approved transporters' which may be a list managed in MDM for all organisations that will be added to the organisations individual transporter options.
claims.note: the owner says "may be", so the MDM management of the approved list is floated rather than settled here; decided point 3 parks it

claims.statement: Approved transporters are not to be worried about for now.
claims.quote: Don't worry about the approved transporters for now.

sources.role: the decision on what the address book stores for an address's type and uses (EUDPA-711): "use" is renamed "role" everywhere, in the record, the API, the code, the copy keys, the tests and the spec, and an address holds the roles it can play on a notification, being place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer, place of destination and branch address. The address book stores roles only and requires at least one; it does not store an address type and ignores one a client sends, the address type being the INS front door's grouping of roles worked out from them. The grouping of roles into sending, receiving and branch is the address book's internal rule rather than part of its API, and it refuses roles from more than one group, and a consignee, importer or place of destination outside the United Kingdom. The list takes role, repeatable and any-of, and searchRole, in place of addressType, use and searchUse. A role a new notification type needs is added in code, each role in exactly one group. Addresses saved before the change are not migrated: after release the addresses collection is dropped in dev and test with CDP tooling and the address book restarted, and locally the stack is restarted. The address book's list and every address picker keep pagination even though the Design Release 2.1 prototype has none, the list API paging with page and pageSize of 1 to 100 defaulting to 25, because organisations in test environments hold thousands of addresses; no requirement to list an organisation's addresses unpaginated is built, which ruling:ian-2026-11-23 point 6 later reads the other way for req-611 and so outranks on that point alone.

sources.role: the owner's decisions: outranks every other source. Search boxes use the real frontend's accessible component with MDM's entries. JavaScript behaviour follows the toolbox rule with graceful degradation; JavaScript-only prototype behaviour, pop-ups included, waits on design in its own theme. Commodity catalogue and search wait on MDM; transporter management waits on requirements; the INS dashboard's summary information waits on its requirements. The overview, review, declaration and confirmation are set-owned, and shared parts change add-only. Where plants has the same page or behaviour, the same increment changes it. Each notification list is reframed in its own frontend. The report groups work as ready or blocked. Claims marked as the orchestrator's apply Sam's principles and are not his rulings; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-templates covers templates and the dashboard narrowing.

claims.statement: Sam rules that the prototype's search and autocomplete controls are not accessible and not production grade, because they are AI-generated prototype code rather than GDS components.

claims.statement: Sam rules that for a search box the precedence is not 'prototype always wins': the component used may be the one already in the real frontends, where it has been deemed accessible.

If it has been, the sort of precedence needs to be a little bit different than prototype always wins. In terms of the component being used, it might be the one that's actually in the frontend or frontends.

claims.statement: Sam rules there is a graceful degradation requirement: CSS and JavaScript may enhance behaviour, but every page must work without JavaScript, so the prototype's way of doing things may not be possible or wanted in the real service.

claims.statement: Sam rules that, as a pre-step for these increments, three questions are answered: is it possible with off-the-shelf GDS; if not, with other complementary off-the-shelf components; if not, why is the atypical thing strongly required. At that point it goes back to design to push back.
claims.quote: Almost as a pre-step for some of these increments, we need to get answers to that stuff: - Is it possible using off-the-shelf GDS? - If it isn't, is it using available, off-the-shelf, other complementary components? - If it isn't, why is this atypical thing strongly required? At that point, we go back to design and say, 'Come on, we don't need this.'

claims.quote: Themes: group the increments into themes based on the evidence.

claims.note: New.

claims.statement: The ruling's DR1 paragraph has an elision marked [...]: what the omitted words said about the DR1 parity backlog is not recorded.
The ruling does not say what makes a difference 'truly exceptional', so when a question for people is warranted is left open.

The ruling limits DR1 use to clashes between 'the real frontend' and the prototype; it does not say which frontend that is, or whether DR1 judgements apply to differences in the INS frontend, the backends or other repos.
The ruling does not say which override wins when a DR1 judgement and a real constraint the prototype cannot express point different ways on the same difference.
The ruling does not say what a real service does where a real constraint overrides the prototype: whether it keeps today's behaviour or matches the prototype as closely as the constraint allows.
The ruling does not say whether a feature or behaviour a real service has that Design Release 2.1 does not show at all counts as a difference to remove, or is left alone.
The ruling does not say what to do where the code two themes need to touch overlaps, so no boundary keeps their pull requests from conflicting.

claims.statement: inc-136 is done: the document upload form has a Document type select between the document reference and the date of issue, opening on "Select one", offering Design release 1's thirteen types in its order, bound to the accompanyingDocumentType field and mandatory when the row is saved, replacing the guess of the type from the filename.
claims.quote: Add a Document type select to the upload form, between the reference and the date of issue, bound to the existing accompanyingDocumentType obligation, with a "Select one" placeholder and DR1's thirteen options in DR1's order, and validate it as mandatory when the row is saved.
claims.note: status is done (commits ffb746cc b7d44ec). The thirteen are listed in finding.prototype: Intra Trade Animal Health Certificate (ITAHC), Veterinary health certificate, Air waybill, Import permit, Letter of authority (Directive 2008/61/EC), Commercial invoice, Sea waybill, Rail waybill, Bill of lading, Catch certificate, Laboratory sampling results for aflatoxin (Reg 2019/1793), Journey log, Other.

claims.statement: The document type options take Design release 1's option text, not the frontend's existing labels: the frontend labelled ITAHC as the bare acronym "ITAHC" where Design release 1 says "Intra Trade Animal Health Certificate (ITAHC)", and the frontend's list carries a fourteenth type, HEALTH_CERTIFICATE, that Design release 1 does not offer to a design-release user.
claims.quote: The claim that "the user-facing labels for every member are already written" is therefore true of the mechanism but not of the wording, and whoever builds the select should take DR1's option text.

claims.statement: Open: the code that orders a merged error summary by field is hand-written in four places, and the order it produces is what the accessibility tests pin; a standalone refactor ticket should lift one shared helper and point all four at it.
claims.quote: Each copy has to be kept in step with its own template by hand, and the resulting summary order is what the accessibility tests pin. ... ACTION: raise a standalone refactor ticket for the shared orderedErrors helper.
claims.note: Not fixed in the increment because it touches three features outside an add-field increment and carries accessibility-ordering regression risk for no behavioural gain. No user-visible behaviour changes.

claims.statement: inc-137 is done: the documents page uses the design system's JavaScript-enhanced file upload — a drop zone, a "Choose file" button, the words "or drop file" and a live region naming the chosen file — rather than rebuilding Design release 1's hand-built markup, because the requirement is the behaviour, not the bespoke classes.
claims.quote: Design release 1 hand-built the same thing in the prototype's own markup, so the requirement is the behaviour, not the bespoke classes; the design-system component satisfies it and should be used instead of rebuilding one.
claims.note: status is done (commits 24b08e2b 2503575). A recorded choice to depart from the prototype's markup while matching its behaviour.

claims.statement: The drop zone shows its own error state when the attachment fails validation, and the plain file input stays behind it as the fallback for a trader whose JavaScript does not run.
claims.quote: The zone's own error state comes with the component, and the unenhanced input stays behind it as the no-JavaScript fallback, so nothing is taken away from a trader whose JavaScript does not run.

claims.statement: Open: nothing tests clearing an earlier client-side oversize error on a second submit. If it went wrong, a trader who hits the oversize error, swaps in a valid file and presses Add another would be left with a stale error reference on the drop-zone button and a stale error style on the input. The team must decide whether the documents client code gets a browser-environment unit-test lane, and if so add the test.
claims.quote:
The failure it would let through: a trader hits the oversize error, swaps in a valid file and presses Add another; if the control/input resolution were wrong the stale aria-describedby="file-hint file-error" would survive on the drop-zone button after clearPreviousClientErrors had already removed the

, leaving a dangling idref, plus a stale govuk-file-upload--error class on the input. ... ACTION: decide whether documents/client/ gets a jsdom unit-test lane
claims.note: DEFERRED: it would be the first jsdom unit test in the frontend repo, a test-infrastructure decision wider than the increment.

claims.statement: Open: nothing proves the documents upload still works with JavaScript off. If the plain input were hidden, a trader without JavaScript would see an empty dashed wrapper and could not attach a document, and the suite would stay green. A JavaScript-off route to the documents page and a test that a plain input is visible and attaches a document are still to be added.
claims.quote: Hide the raw input for real — app CSS such as .govuk-file-upload-wrapper .govuk-file-upload { display: none }, or a {% if %} around the macro call — and a JS-off trader is left with a dashed empty wrapper and no way to attach a document, while the suite stays green. This increment renames that test to what it really pins; the missing coverage stays open.
claims.note: DEFERRED because reaching the documents page with JavaScript off needs a no-JavaScript variant of the shared journey set-up (country of origin answered through the native select rather than the type-ahead), which touches every feature's set-up.

claims.statement: inc-138 is done in code: the accepted document size rises from 10 MB to Design release 1's 50MB, with the hint bullet and the oversize error message changed to match.
claims.quote: Raise the accepted file size from 10 MB to 50MB and change the hint bullet and the oversize error message to match.
claims.note: status is done (commits 3fe7da19 50ff56f), but the first open question says it must not be deployed until the platform ingress cap is confirmed.

claims.statement: The size limit's unit is written the Design release 1 way, "50MB" with no space, rather than the frontend's former "10 MB" with a space.
claims.quote: Settle the unit in the same edit — Design release 1 writes "50MB" with no space where the frontend writes "10 MB" with one.
claims.note: Inferred that the unspaced form was adopted: the difference asks for the unit to be settled, and openQuestions[0] names the fallback as "only the unit/label correction ('10 MB' -> '10MB') lands".

claims.statement: The 50MB limit depends on the hosting platform: the request-body cap on the platform's ingress and on whatever receives the upload must allow at least 50MB first, or a large file is refused by the infrastructure and the trader gets a platform error page instead of a validation message.
claims.quote: the request-body cap on the hosting platform's ingress and on whatever receives the upload has to be raised to at least 50MB first, otherwise a large file will be rejected by the infrastructure before the service sees it and the trader will get a platform error page instead of a validation message.
claims.note: Banded needs-backend as the nearest band; the dependency is the platform ingress cap, not a backend service change.

claims.statement: Blocking before deploy and unconfirmed: the CDP nginx ingress request-body cap in front of the animals frontend must be confirmed as at least 50,001,024 bytes. Nothing in the workspace confirms it, and the tests repo still records it as 10 MiB.
claims.quote: BLOCKING BEFORE DEPLOY — has the CDP nginx ingress request-body cap in front of trade-imports-animals-frontend been raised to at least 50,001,024 bytes (MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES)?

claims.statement: The backend half of the 50MB dependency is met: the animals backend accepts files of 50MB, requests of 51MB, and an uploader maximum of 52428800 bytes, so the platform ingress is the only limit still outstanding.
claims.quote: The backend half of the dependency IS met and was verified: repos/trade-imports-animals-backend/src/main/resources/application.yml:29 sets spring.servlet.multipart.max-file-size to 50MB, :30 max-request-size 51MB, :45 cdp.uploader.max-file-size 52428800. So the ingress is the single outstanding limit.

claims.statement: If deployed before the ingress cap is raised, every file between 10,485,760 and 50,000,000 bytes passes the service's checks and is then refused by the ingress: the trader gets a platform 413 error page and loses the document type, reference and date of issue they typed, which is worse than today's inline 10 MB error that keeps them.
claims.ref: backlog.json inc-138, openQuestions[0], CONSEQUENCE IF DEPLOYED UNCONFIRMED
claims.quote: The trader gets a platform 413 error page and loses the document type, reference and issue date they had typed, because handleOversizePayload (controller.js:309-311) is an onPreResponse extension and never runs for a request that never reaches hapi. That is strictly worse than today's inline 'The selected file must be smaller than 10 MB' with the metadata preserved — a user-visible regression across a 5x band of file sizes.

claims.statement: A configurable file-size limit read from an environment setting was considered and rejected for this increment: a default of 10 gives no parity anywhere and leaves the end-to-end tests not knowing which limit is in force, and a default of 50 ships the regression anyway.
claims.quote: The reviewed alternative — sourcing MAX_FILE_SIZE_MB from convict in src/config/config.js behind DOCUMENT_MAX_FILE_SIZE_MB so the app limit can be flipped independently — was rejected as a fix for this increment: with a default of 10 the increment achieves no parity in any environment and the E2E suite can no longer know which limit is in force, and with a default of 50 the regression ships anyway

claims.statement: Action for the service team: confirm the ingress body-size cap is at least 50,001,024 and record the confirmation against EUDPA-518 before the branch is deployed; if it cannot be raised, hold the merge and split the increment so only the unit and label correction ('10 MB' to '10MB') lands.
claims.ref: backlog.json inc-138, openQuestions[0], ACTION FOR THE SERVICE TEAM
claims.quote: ACTION FOR THE SERVICE TEAM: confirm the ingress proxy-body-size in front of this service is >= 50,001,024 and record the confirmation (ticket or config reference) against EUDPA-518 before this branch is deployed to CDP; if it cannot be raised, hold the merge and split the increment so only the unit/label correction ('10 MB' -> '10MB') lands.
claims.note: The ingress is a CDP platform setting owned outside every repo in the workspace.

claims.statement: Open: the frontend container's memory headroom under the 50MB limit is unknown. Each in-flight upload is held about three times in memory (about 150 MB at 50MB), nothing bounds it, and a few concurrent large uploads could crash the instance and drop every journey on it. The team must decide whether to confirm and record the container memory and concurrency it supports, or to stream uploads instead of buffering them, sized as its own increment.
claims.quote: A handful of concurrent large certificate uploads on a small CDP container would exhaust the heap and OOM-restart the pod, dropping every in-flight journey on that instance, not only the uploads. ... ACTION: decide which, and size it as its own increment.

claims.note: Inferred from the claim setting any DocumentType without consulting the notification.

claims.statement: Accompanying documents are stored in their own MongoDB collection, accompanying_documents, apart from the notification record, and are linked to it by notificationReferenceNumber.
claims.quote:
@Document(collection = "accompanying_documents") ... @Indexed
  private String notificationReferenceNumber;

claims.statement: An accompanying document records: id, version, notificationReferenceNumber, uploadId, correlationId, documentType, documentReference, dateOfIssue, scanStatus, claimed, files, created, updated and expireAt.
claims.quote: private String id; ... private Long version; ... private String notificationReferenceNumber; ... private String uploadId; ... private String correlationId; private DocumentType documentType; private String documentReference; private LocalDate dateOfIssue; private ScanStatus scanStatus; ... private boolean claimed = false; ... private List<UploadedFile> files = new ArrayList<>(); ... private Instant created; ... private Instant updated; private Instant expireAt;

claims.statement: Each accompanying document's uploadId is unique, and so is its correlationId.
An accompanying document is versioned for optimistic locking, and records when it was created and last updated.
A document holds a list of uploaded files, and is unclaimed until the trader's details are supplied.
The date of issue is a calendar date with no time, stored as a YYYY-MM-DD string.
claims.quote: private LocalDate dateOfIssue;
claims.note: The string storage is stated in design-notes.md line 8: 'Calendar dates (arrivalDate, exitDate, a document's dateOfIssue) are LocalDate, stored by LocalDateStringConverters as YYYY-MM-DD strings.'

claims.statement: The trader supplies three details for a document when claiming it: the document type, the document reference and the date of issue, and all three are required.
claims.quote: @NotNull ... DocumentType documentType, @NotBlank ... String documentReference, @NotNull ... LocalDate dateOfIssue

claims.statement: A document reference must not be blank.
claims.quote: @NotBlank

claims.statement: A document reference is at most 58 characters long.
claims.quote: @Size(max = ClaimUploadRequest.REFERENCE_MAX_LENGTH) ... static final int REFERENCE_MAX_LENGTH = 58;

claims.statement: A document reference may contain only letters, digits, spaces, full stops, slashes and hyphens.
claims.quote: static final String REFERENCE_PATTERN = "^[A-Za-z0-9 ./-]*$";
claims.note: The Javadoc gives the examples an air waybill '125-12345675' and a TRACES certificate 'CHEDA.GB.2026.1234567'.

claims.statement: The date of issue has no range rule in the backend: any valid date, past or future, is accepted.
claims.note: Inferred from the only constraint being @NotNull; no @Past or @PastOrPresent.

claims.statement: The backend's validation errors carry no user-facing messages for the document details: the constraints use the default messages, so the wording a trader sees comes from the frontend.
claims.note: Inferred from no message attribute on any constraint.

claims.statement: An upload session is a separate record in its own collection, document_upload_sessions, holding the notification reference number, the uploadId, the correlationId and when it was created.
claims.quote: @Document(collection = "document_upload_sessions") ... private String notificationReferenceNumber; ... private String uploadId; ... private String correlationId; ... private Instant created;

claims.statement: An upload session's uploadId is unique, and so is its correlationId.
An upload session expires and is removed 24 hours after it was created, whether or not anything was uploaded through it.
When registering an upload session, the uploadId is required, must be 1 to 100 characters and may contain only letters, digits, full stops, underscores and hyphens.
When registering an upload session, the correlationId is required, must be 1 to 100 characters and may contain only letters, digits, full stops, underscores and hyphens.

The caller opens the cdp-uploader session itself and then registers it here; the correlationId is the identifier the caller threaded through cdp-uploader's metadata, which the scan callback echoes back so the result can be matched to the session.
claims.quote: Request body for registering an upload session the caller has already opened with cdp-uploader. ... "Identifier the caller threaded through cdp-uploader's metadata, which the scan callback echoes back so the result can be matched to this session"

claims.statement: POST /notifications/{referenceNumber}/document-uploads registers an upload session for a notification and answers 201 Created with the session (notificationReferenceNumber, uploadId, correlationId) and a Location header of <base URL>/document-uploads/<uploadId>.
claims.quote: @PostMapping("/notifications/{referenceNumber}/document-uploads") ... return ResponseEntity.created(location).body(UploadSessionDto.from(session)); ... return URI.create(baseUrl + "/document-uploads/" + uploadId);

claims.statement: A second registration with an uploadId or a correlationId already in use is refused as a conflict, with the message 'An upload session already exists for uploadId <uploadId> or correlationId <correlationId>'.
Registering a session writes no accompanying document: a notification gains a document only when a claim or a scan result arrives.
claims.quote:
UploadSession session = UploadSession.builder() ... .build();

    return saveSession(session);
claims.note: design-notes.md line 62 gives the reason: the frontend opens a session every time it paints the upload page.

claims.statement: A notification can hold several upload sessions at once, because sessions are unique only by uploadId and correlationId, never by notification.
claims.quote:
@Indexed
  private String notificationReferenceNumber;
claims.note: Inferred from the notification index being non-unique; design-notes.md line 63 states it: 'A notification can hold several open sessions'.

claims.statement: Every document endpoint except the scan callback needs the Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id header, and checks that the notification belongs to that organisation before doing anything.
claims.quote: @RequestHeader(TraderOrganisationHeaderFilter.ORGANISATION_ID_HEADER) String organisationId ... notificationService.requireTraderAccess(referenceNumber, organisationId);

claims.statement: For endpoints addressed by uploadId (claim, get, delete, download), the organisation check finds the notification through the upload session, so an uploadId with no session is refused as not found with 'No upload session found with uploadId: <uploadId>'.

Because uploadId endpoints reach the notification through the session, and sessions expire after 24 hours, a document whose session has expired can no longer be read, downloaded, deleted or claimed through the API: each answers 404.
claims.quote:
private static final String SESSION_RETENTION_PERIOD = "24h"; ... .orElseThrow(() -> new NotFoundException(
            "No upload session found with uploadId: " + uploadId));
claims.note: Inferred from the two facts together; not stated anywhere. The list endpoint, which goes by notification, still returns such a document. The reconciler may want to treat this as a constraint on how long a draft's documents stay usable.

claims.statement: GET /notifications/{referenceNumber}/document-upload-sessions/{correlationId} returns the upload session a notification opened under that correlationId, with 200, so the browser's return to the upload page can find it.
claims.quote: @GetMapping("/notifications/{referenceNumber}/document-upload-sessions/{correlationId}") ... description = "Returns the upload session a notification opened under a correlationId")

claims.statement: A session is looked up by notification and correlationId together, so a correlationId cannot reach another notification's session; a miss answers 404 with 'No upload session found for notification <ref> with correlationId: <correlationId>'.
claims.quote:
.findByNotificationReferenceNumberAndCorrelationId(
            notificationReferenceNumber, correlationId)
        .orElseThrow(() -> new NotFoundException(
            "No upload session found for notification " + notificationReferenceNumber
                + " with correlationId: " + correlationId));

claims.statement: On the register and get-session endpoints, the reference number in the path must match the notification reference number pattern, and the correlationId path value must be 1 to 100 letters, digits, full stops, underscores or hyphens.
claims.quote: private static final String UPLOAD_SESSION_IDENTIFIER_PATTERN = "^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,100}$"; ... @PathVariable @Pattern(regexp = ReferenceNumberGenerator.REFERENCE_NUMBER_PATTERN)
claims.note: The reference number pattern itself is in the notification package (part 2).

claims.statement: POST /document-uploads/{uploadId}/claim attaches the trader's document details (type, reference, date of issue) to a registered upload, marks the document claimed and answers 200 with the document.
Claiming can be repeated: each claim replaces the type, reference and date of issue on the same document, so a repeated claim never creates a second document.
claims.quote:
AccompanyingDocument document = existingOrNewDocumentFor(session); ... return accompanyingDocumentRepository
        .findByCorrelationId(session.getCorrelationId())
claims.note: design-notes.md line 69: 'Claiming is repeatable: it replaces the details, so a repeated claim cannot produce a second document.' This is how a trader changes a document's details.

claims.statement: A claim can arrive before the scan result: if no document exists yet for the session it creates one with scan status PENDING and no files.
claims.quote:
.orElseGet(() -> AccompanyingDocument.builder() ... .scanStatus(ScanStatus.PENDING)
            .files(new ArrayList<>())

claims.statement: A claim does not check the scan status: a document can be claimed while its scan is PENDING or after it was REJECTED.
claims.quote:
AccompanyingDocument document = existingOrNewDocumentFor(session);

    document.setDocumentType(request.documentType());
claims.note: Inferred from claimUpload reading no scanStatus.

claims.statement: A claim does not check the notification's status, so the backend lets documents be claimed on a notification in any state, including a submitted one.
claims.note: Inferred: requireTraderAccess checks only the organisation in what this part reads. Registering, deleting and the scan callback likewise read no notification status.

claims.statement: POST /document-uploads/{pathSegment}/scan-results receives cdp-uploader's antivirus scan result and answers 204 No Content.
claims.quote: @PostMapping("/document-uploads/{pathSegment}/scan-results") ... description = "Receives the cdp-uploader antivirus scan result callback") ... return ResponseEntity.noContent().build();

claims.statement: The scan callback ignores its path segment and finds the session by the correlationId in the payload's metadata.
claims.quote: @param pathSegment the fixed segment the session's callback URL was opened with ... return metadata.get("correlationId");
claims.note: design-notes.md line 73: the path variable is always the literal 'pending'.

claims.statement: A scan callback with no correlationId, or a blank one, is refused as a bad request with 'Scan callback missing required correlationId in metadata'.
claims.quote:
throw new BadRequestException(
          "Scan callback missing required correlationId in metadata");

claims.statement: A scan callback whose correlationId matches no session is refused as not found with 'No upload session found with correlationId: <correlationId>', so a result arriving after the session expired or was deleted writes nothing.
A scan result replaces the document's files with the files in the result and sets its scan status, creating the document if the claim has not arrived yet.
claims.quote:
AccompanyingDocument document = existingOrNewDocumentFor(session); ... document.setFiles(mapUploadedFiles(payload));
    document.setScanStatus(resolveScanStatus(payload));

claims.statement: A document created by the scan callback is unclaimed and has no type, reference or date of issue until the trader claims it.
claims.quote: "Whether the trader's document details have been supplied; an upload the user walked away from stays unclaimed"

claims.statement: A scan result fails closed: the document is COMPLETE only when the result says exactly zero files were rejected; a missing or non-zero rejected count marks it REJECTED.
A document's scan status is PENDING (uploaded and awaiting antivirus scanning), COMPLETE (scanned and clean) or REJECTED (virus or malware detected).
claims.quote:
"File has been uploaded and is awaiting antivirus scanning")
  PENDING, ... "Antivirus scan completed successfully — file is clean")
  COMPLETE, ... "Antivirus scan rejected the file (virus or malware detected)")
  REJECTED

claims.statement: A document's scan status moves from PENDING to COMPLETE or REJECTED only through a scan callback, and a later callback for the same session can move it again, since each one overwrites the status.
claims.quote: .scanStatus(ScanStatus.PENDING) ... document.setScanStatus(resolveScanStatus(payload));
claims.note: Inferred from handleScanResult being the only writer of scanStatus besides the PENDING default.

claims.statement: The scan result's form section is read leniently: only values carrying a fileId are recorded as files, an object-shaped value with no fileId is dropped with a warning naming the field, and other values are ignored.
claims.note: mechanism: filters cdp-uploader's echoed form fields down to file entries.

claims.statement: The scan result payload carries an uploadStatus, a metadata map, a form section and numberOfRejectedFiles; each file entry carries fileId, filename, contentType, fileStatus, contentLength, checksumSha256, detectedContentType, s3Key, s3Bucket, hasError, errorCode and errorMessage, and unknown fields are tolerated.
